questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find things you have lost at home
Why we forget things and how to remember better
How Chinese students prepare for maths exams
Why some people have photographic memories
questions.why: Rob says they'll find out why we forget the things we've learned, and they hear rules for remembering.

questions.q: What does Rob say about his own memory?
options: He never forgets anything he reads
He remembers names but forgets faces
He has a photographic memory
He remembers faces but not names
questions.why: Rob says he can remember faces but has a terrible memory for names.

questions.q: What is Dr Jared Horvath's first rule for remembering?
options: Repetition is key
Always write things down
Learn things only once
Study late at night
questions.why: He says, 'Rule number one is repetition is key.'

questions.q: Why does Dr Horvath mention his middle name, Cuney?
options: To show that unusual names are easy to forget
To explain how he got interested in memory
To show that links help us remember
To say that he often forgets people's names
questions.why: He says if he meets someone named Cuney he'll never forget, because he has an immediate link.

questions.q: What is Dr Horvath's second rule?
options: We remember things we hear only once
We remember what we focus on
We remember things better when tired
We remember names better than numbers
questions.why: He says, 'rule two then becomes, we remember what we focus on'.

questions.q: What does Georgina say about cramming for exams?
options: It helped her get the best marks in class
She never did it because it was too tiring
She still does it before important meetings
She did it, but it didn't work for her
questions.why: She remembers staying up late to revise the night before an exam, 'but it didn't work!'

questions.q: What did Dr Horvath's research find about students who cram?
options: They remember almost everything for years
They get better results than other students
They forget about 90% within three days
They forget everything within one hour
questions.why: Rob says they forget around 90% of what they studied within 72 hours.

questions.q: What does Dr Horvath mean by 'deep learning'?
options: Understanding a few things deeply
Memorising a hundred facts as quickly as possible
Repeating information exactly, like a parrot
Studying for many hours without a break
questions.why: Instead of remembering a hundred things, he'll give you ten things to describe deeply and look at in new ways.
